summary: Config surge: aggressive optimizer profile triggered tenant KPIs — mitigation & controlled rollback walkthrough
description:
Issue summary:
An aggressive optimizer profile (experimental profile 'aggr-prefetch-v3') was enabled for BrightHealth AI tenant in Dedicated capacity. Within minutes we observed P95/P99 tail latency spikes and intermittent 5xx responses for long-sequence streaming requests.

Impact:
- Customer-facing latency increased: 95th latency rose from ~120ms to ~2.7s for token streaming paths.
- Spike in 5xx errors (503/504) and a few OOMs on one GPU node in their Dedicated pool.
- Production traffic was degraded for ~18 minutes before mitigations.

Environment:
- Dedicated GPU pool: dhp-dedicated-us-east-4 (A100s), tenant BrightHealth AI.
- Model: redwood-v2-7b pinned at version 2026-02-18.
- Optimizer profile applied: aggr-prefetch-v3 (changes: prefix KV prefetch enabled + target_batch_size from auto->256 + delayed flush window).

Steps to reproduce (approx):
1) Apply optimizer profile 'aggr-prefetch-v3' via console -> tenant overrides.
2) Send long-sequence streaming requests (~2048 tokens) with concurrent clients at 30 RPS.
3) Observe serving/runtime metrics for request queue length and KV cache hit/miss.

Observed behavior:
- Sustained queue growth on a subset of shards.
- KV cache evictions climbed rapidly; prefetch thrash and increased host<->GPU PCIe traffic.
- Autoscaler did not immediately pick up the pressure due to burst policy thresholds.

Expected behavior:
- Optimizer profile should improve tail latency for typical workloads and not cause sustained queue growth or OOMs.

Logs & metrics:
- Grafana dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/tenant-brighthealth/tenant-serving-overview?from=2026-03-10T14:00:00Z&to=2026-03-10T15:00:00Z
- Error logs sample: request_id=rcq_9f7a, 2026-03-10T14:07:12Z, "kv_cache_eviction_rate=0.86, queue_len=72, gpu_mem_free=1.2GB"
- Node OOM events: kube://dhp-node-17 (oom_kill)

Customer impact note:
Customer reported a critical degradation affecting a staging-to-prod migration gate for a marketing launch. They requested immediate rollback help and confirmation of a safe rollback path that avoids cold-start regressions.
comments: Support (2026-03-10 14:12 UTC) - Asha Patel: Acknowledged. Opening incident, prioritizing P1. I requested immediate snapshot of optimizer config and tenant traffic split. Asked SRE for node health and autoscaler logs.

SRE (2026-03-10 14:18 UTC) - Jamie Liu: Observed increased PCIe and host memory churn on node dhp-node-17; several pods showing high iowait. Autoscaler didn't scale because average CPU across pool remained below threshold; queue growth happened on per-shard basis.

Customer (2026-03-10 14:22 UTC) - BrightHealth Oncall: We rolled the change back from our side but see residual 5xx on some requests. Need confirmation the profile is fully disabled per-tenant and whether traffic was routed to fallback model variants.

Support (2026-03-10 14:28 UTC) - Marco Ruiz: Confirmed profile unset at tenant override layer. Initiating controlled per-tenant snapshot restore and staged traffic isolation to remove prefetch hooks. Also applied temporary rate-limit to tenant token throughput to prevent immediate re-thrashing.

SRE (2026-03-10 14:40 UTC) - Jamie Liu: Performed a hot-snapshot restore of the last stable optimizer snapshot (2026-03-09T02:12Z) for BrightHealth tenant on 3 affected shards. Evictions fell and queue length returned to normal within 9 minutes.

Customer (2026-03-10 15:05 UTC) - BrightHealth Oncall: Confirmed latency recovered and 5xx reduced to baseline. Thanks. Requesting a short post-incident summary and recommended safe profile rollout checklist.

Support (2026-03-11 09:10 UTC) - Marco Ruiz: Created this ticket to capture the mitigation steps, findings, and recommended preflight checks. Added follow-up tasks for engineering to harden circuit-breakers.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis: Aggressive prefetch + larger target batch size caused pathological cache churn for long-tail sequence distribution used by this tenant.
Telemetry shows per-shard queue growth rather than cluster-wide CPU pressure—indicates scheduler/placement sensitivity to sequence-length skew.
Autoscaler logic thresholds are average-based and lacked per-shard burst response—contributed to 10-15 minute reaction lag.
No evidence of code regressions in model runtime; related PR (runtime#4821) was experimental flags-only and toggles look correct.
KV cache metrics show increased eviction_rate from 0.05 -> 0.86 during incident window.
One node hit OOM; root cause was combined host memory pressure from prefetch buffers and larger batch kernel memory reservation.
Fallback routing did not trigger because the fallback policy only matches when node health is 'unhealthy' not on per-shard queue thresholds.
actions_taken: Confirmed tenant override and immediately unset optimizer profile 'aggr-prefetch-v3'.
Applied temporary tenant-level token throughput throttle (reduce to 60% of baseline) to avoid immediate re-thrash during recovery window.
Hot restored optimizer snapshot (2026-03-09T02:12Z) to 3 affected shards to rehydrate stable KV profile and kernel settings.
Isolated routing: drained new connections from 2 noisy shards and rebalanced traffic across spare capacity nodes.
Filed internal engineering ticket to add per-shard queue-based autoscaler trigger (see linked issue SUP-82401).
workaround: Step 1: Disable tenant optimizer override from Console -> Tenant -> Optimizer Overrides.
Step 2: If 5xx persists, apply immediate tenant token throttle: support API POST /admin/tenant/throttle {tenant_id, pct=60}.
Step 3: Hot-restore last-known-good optimizer snapshot using admin CLI: redwood admin snapshot restore --tenant <id> --snapshot 2026-03-09T02:12Z
Step 4: If node OOM observed, cordon and drain the affected node and restart pods after verifying kernel memory release.
resolution: Rolled back tenant optimizer override, restored last stable optimizer snapshot to affected shards, applied temporary throughput throttling, and rebalanced traffic. Latency and error rates returned to baseline. Engineering to implement per-shard autoscaler triggers and a per-tenant optimizer gating rule before reintroducing aggressive profiles.
follow_up_tasks: ENG-1258: Implement per-shard queue-length autoscaler trigger and test under synthetic long-sequence workload.
ENG-1259: Add optimizer profile gating checks in Console UI and disallow 'aggr-prefetch-v3' globally until safety validation completes.
DOCS-77: Publish a 'Safe Rollout' checklist for optimizer profiles (including prefetched memory budget estimation and per-tenant shadow runs).
SRE-404: Update incident runbook to include hot-snapshot restore steps and tenant throttle API examples.
customer_communication: 2026-03-10 14:14 UTC: Acknowledged incident and escalated to SRE. Requested temporary mitigation permission.
2026-03-10 14:30 UTC: Informed customer we were unsetting the optimizer override and applying a short throttle while we restore snapshots.
2026-03-10 15:08 UTC: Notified customer that metrics returned to baseline and recommended waiting 24h before reintroducing changes and to run the preflight checklist.
recommended_preflight_checks: Run tenant-specific synthetic workload that matches 95th/99th sequence length distribution for 30 minutes.
Estimate KV cache memory impact via 'optimizer-sim --profile aggr-prefetch-v3 --tenant <id>' and confirm < 40% of host spare memory.
Enable profile in shadow mode for 1% traffic for 6 hours and monitor eviction_rate and queue_len per shard.
Ensure autoscaler per-shard triggers are enabled or manual escalation plan is in place.
